children: Private credit funds saw signs of stabilizing in September as redemption requests from individual investors eased and investment performance improved after a difficult start to the year, the Financial Times reported Sunday.
Flagship funds managed by Apollo Global
reported lower withdrawal requests in the third quarter, while redemptions at Blackstone’s
large private credit fund held roughly steady. The figures suggest some of the anxiety over corporate defaults and credit quality may be receding.

For investors, the improvement could reduce pressure on major alternative asset managers after months of heavy withdrawals. But the recovery remains incomplete. Funds continue to limit redemptions, new investment has been sluggish and weaker asset growth could restrain management and performance fees.
Ares Strategic Income Fund said investors requested withdrawals equal to 13.1% of shares during the third quarter, down from 14.4% in the prior period.

At Apollo’s roughly $15 billion flagship debt fund, redemption requests fell to 14.7% from 16.8%. Requests at BlackRock’s HPS corporate lending fund declined to 11.5% from 13.3%, while Blackstone’s $43 billion flagship private credit vehicle held steady at about 10%.

Despite the improvement, investors seeking to leave the funds still face a backlog. The four vehicles fulfilled less than half of requested withdrawals on average as redemption limits remained in place.

Pressure began building last year as falling interest rates threatened private credit returns and several high-profile corporate failures raised questions about lending standards. By the second quarter of 2026, all four major funds had capped quarterly redemptions at 5% of fund value.

Across 13 non-traded business development companies that have reported third-quarter results, investors requested $9.6 billion in withdrawals, according to RA Stanger. That represented 10.1% of fund value, down from 11.2% in the second quarter.
Private credit performance also has improved in recent months, although the asset class continues to trail the broader debt market this year.

The slowdown in withdrawals offers some relief for private capital managers, but earnings pressure may persist. Limited inflows and constrained asset growth could keep management-fee expansion weak, while softer performance is expected to reduce incentive fees.

title: Private credit redemption pressure eases as fund performance improves
